manifest_row <- function(supplement_id) {
  row <- manifest %>% filter(.data$supplement_id == .env$supplement_id)
  if (nrow(row) != 1L) stop("Expected one manifest row for ", supplement_id)
  row
}

read_supp <- function(supplement_id) {
  row <- manifest_row(supplement_id)
  read_csv(
    file.path(DATA, row$filename[[1]]),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    progress = FALSE
  )
}

show_table <- function(data, rows = 10L, columns = 12L) {
  rmarkdown::paged_table(
    data,
    options = list(
      rows.print = min(rows, nrow(data)),
      cols.print = min(columns, ncol(data))
    )
  )
}

sha256_file <- function(path) {
  output <- system2("sha256sum", path, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  if (length(output) != 1L) stop("Could not hash ", path)
  strsplit(output, "[[:space:]]+")[[1]][[1]]
}

species_label <- function(x) {
  text <- as.character(x)
  ifelse(grepl("^D\\. ", text), text, paste("D.", text))
}

figure_path <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(FIGURES, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing figure: ", path, ". Run `make figures`.")
  path
}

escape_html <- function(value, attribute = FALSE) {
  htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(value), attribute = attribute)
}

format_inline <- function(value) {
  escaped <- escape_html(value)
  gsub("`([^`]+)`", "<code>\\1</code>", escaped, perl = TRUE)
}

auxiliary_paths <- file.path(FIGURES, auxiliary_manifest$png)
if (any(!file.exists(auxiliary_paths))) {
  stop(
    "Missing auxiliary figure files: ",
    paste(basename(auxiliary_paths[!file.exists(auxiliary_paths)]), collapse = ", "),
    ". Run `make figures`."
  )
}

stopifnot(
  nrow(manifest) == 43L,
  identical(manifest$supplement_id, sprintf("S%02d", seq_len(43))),
  nrow(auxiliary_manifest) == 5L
)

This is a read-only researcher-facing view over the controlled study release. The CSV files and their hashes remain the data authority. Code chunks make the filters and equations visible; the report does not overwrite a source table, review decision, or publication dataset.

Claim boundaries. Genome-size values are conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C estimates, not direct independently measured species C-values. Their assay and conversion evidence is isolated in the calibration proof below. The anchor is 16.462167689 pg/1C (16.1 Gbp / 0.978 Gbp per pg). The LTR terminal:internal statistic is a mapping/deletion-footprint proxy, not a direct ectopic-recombination, solo-LTR, or DNA-loss rate. Cell and nucleus summaries describe the reviewed upper tail of observed erythrocytes and their intervals are conditional on the observed animals and images. Current path analyses are exploratory and do not orient a unique causal arrow.

Study report

Guide and dataset index

What is included

  • TE34: 34 species with accession-linked genomic resources.
  • Path24: 24 species with finalized conditional genome-size, cell, and nucleus data.
  • overlap21: the exact 21-species intersection; no TE or phenotype values are imputed.
  • S01–S43: controlled CSV supplements with source/output SHA-256 hashes.
  • Figures: the exact current ggplot figures built by scripts/publication/build_gbe_figures.R.

The report shows compact species-level tables directly. Large object- and element-level tables remain downloadable CSVs so the HTML stays responsive.

manifest %>%
  select(
    supplement_id,
    analysis_section,
    title,
    release_status,
    manuscript_use,
    rows,
    columns,
    filename,
    output_sha256
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 9)

Exact ggplot code and current figure

The following collapsed source chunk is the production ggplot code, read from the single figure builder rather than copied into this report.

# Figure 1: focal time tree, analysis design, genomic resources, and dnaPipeTE QC.
path_traits <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S04_path_analysis_traits24.csv")
tree_audit_edges <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S38_phylogeny_edges.csv")
tree_audit_nodes <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S39_phylogeny_nodes.csv")
tree_path <- file.path(DATA, "trees", "desmognathus_time_tree_path24_v1.nwk")
path_tree <- read.tree(tree_path)
path_tree <- rotateConstr(
  path_tree,
  phylogenetic_species_order(path_tree$tip.label)
)

tip_count <- Ntip(path_tree)
node_count <- Nnode(path_tree)
root_distance <- node.depth.edgelength(path_tree)
root_age <- max(root_distance[seq_len(tip_count)])
node_age <- root_age - root_distance
node_y <- node.height(path_tree)

tree_horizontal <- tibble(
  parent = path_tree$edge[, 1],
  child = path_tree$edge[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    x = node_age[parent],
    xend = node_age[child],
    y = node_y[child],
    yend = node_y[child]
  )
tree_vertical <- tibble(parent = sort(unique(path_tree$edge[, 1]))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x = node_age[parent],
    ymin = min(node_y[path_tree$edge[path_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]]),
    ymax = max(node_y[path_tree$edge[path_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]])
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
tree_tips <- tibble(
  node = seq_len(tip_count),
  tree_tip = path_tree$tip.label,
  x = 0,
  y = node_y[seq_len(tip_count)]
) %>%
  left_join(
    path_traits %>% select(species, tree_tip),
    by = "tree_tip",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

audit_tip_labels <- tree_audit_nodes %>%
  filter(is_tip) %>%
  pull(tip_label)
if (
  tip_count != 24L ||
    node_count != 23L ||
    nrow(tree_horizontal) != 46L ||
    nrow(tree_vertical) != 23L ||
    nrow(tree_audit_edges) != 46L ||
    nrow(tree_audit_nodes) != 47L ||
    any(is.na(tree_tips$species)) ||
    !setequal(path_tree$tip.label, path_traits$tree_tip) ||
    !setequal(path_tree$tip.label, audit_tip_labels) ||
    !isTRUE(all.equal(
      tree_horizontal$x - tree_horizontal$xend,
      path_tree$edge.length,
      tolerance = 1e-12,
      check.attributes = FALSE
    )) ||
    abs(root_age - max(tree_audit_nodes$root_distance_myr)) > 1e-4
) {
  stop("Path24 figure references require the exact audited 24-tip time tree")
}
if (
  !is.rooted(path_tree) ||
    !is.binary(path_tree) ||
    !is.ultrametric(path_tree, tol = 1e-6) ||
    any(path_tree$edge.length < 0)
) {
  stop("Path24 figure references require a rooted, binary, time-scaled tree with nonnegative edges")
}

phylogeny_a <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(
    data = tree_horizontal,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    linewidth = 0.35,

  ) +

  ) +

    hjust = 0,

    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  scale_x_reverse(
    breaks = c(30, 20, 10, 0),
    limits = c(root_age, -14),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, tip_count + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Time before present (Ma; as supplied)", y = NULL) +
  theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 4, unit = "pt")
  )
overview_annotations <- read_supp(
  "Supplementary_Data_S42_te_bonsai_tip_annotations.csv"
)
overview_quality <- read_supp(
  "Supplementary_Data_S24_nuclear_iod_quality_balance.csv"
)
overview_traits <- path_traits %>%
  transmute(
    species = sub("^D\\. ", "", species),
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored,
    genome_size_pg_ci_low,
    genome_size_pg_ci_high,
    n_genome_size_images,
    n_genome_size_specimens
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    overview_annotations %>%
      select(species, reproductive_strategy, reproductive_strategy_label),
    by = "species",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    overview_quality %>%
      transmute(
        species = sub("^D\\. ", "", species),
        passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds
      ),
    by = "species",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )
if (
  nrow(overview_traits) != 21L ||
    !identical(
      as.integer(table(factor(
        overview_traits$reproductive_strategy,
        levels = te_strategy_levels
      ))),
      c(6L, 13L, 2L)
    ) ||
    any(is.na(overview_traits$passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds))
) {
  stop("Figure 1 requires the exact 21-species, 6/13/2 integrated panel")
}

overview_tree <- prune_source_tree(overview_traits$species)
overview_tip_count <- Ntip(overview_tree)
overview_node_y <- node.height(overview_tree)
overview_edges <- reorder.phylo(overview_tree, "cladewise")$edge
overview_depth <- numeric(overview_tip_count + Nnode(overview_tree))
overview_root <- setdiff(overview_edges[, 1], overview_edges[, 2])
if (length(overview_root) != 1L) stop("Figure 1 overview tree requires one root")
for (edge_index in seq_len(nrow(overview_edges))) {
  parent <- overview_edges[edge_index, 1]
  child <- overview_edges[edge_index, 2]
  overview_depth[child] <- overview_depth[parent] + 1
}
overview_tip_x <- max(overview_depth) + 0.5
overview_tree_horizontal <- tibble(
  parent = overview_tree$edge[, 1],
  child = overview_tree$edge[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    x = overview_depth[parent],
    xend = if_else(child <= overview_tip_count, overview_tip_x, overview_depth[child]),
    y = overview_node_y[child],
    yend = overview_node_y[child]
  )
overview_tree_vertical <- tibble(
  parent = sort(unique(overview_tree$edge[, 1]))
) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x = overview_depth[parent],
    ymin = min(overview_node_y[
      overview_tree$edge[overview_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]
    ]),
    ymax = max(overview_node_y[
      overview_tree$edge[overview_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]
    ])
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
overview_tips <- tibble(
  species = overview_tree$tip.label,
  x = overview_tip_x,
  y = overview_node_y[seq_len(overview_tip_count)]
) %>%
  left_join(overview_traits, by = "species", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(
    reproductive_strategy = factor(
      reproductive_strategy,
      levels = te_strategy_levels
    ),
    genome_support = factor(
      case_when(
        !passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds ~ "Quality-balance caution",
        n_genome_size_images == 1L & n_genome_size_specimens == 1L ~
          "One image and animal",
        TRUE ~ "Balanced multi-image support"
      ),
      levels = c(
        "Balanced multi-image support",
        "One image and animal",
        "Quality-balance caution"
      )
    ),
    display_species = species_label(species)
  )
overview_order <- phylogenetic_species_order(overview_traits$species)
if (
  overview_tip_count != 21L ||
    !identical(overview_tree$tip.label[order(overview_tips$y)], overview_order) ||
    any(is.na(overview_tips$genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored))
) {
  stop("Figure 1 species tracks must share the exact overlap21 tree-tip order")
}

overview_order_composition <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT,
    "analyses",
    "01_transposable_elements",
    "data",
    "te_order_composition.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(species %in% overview_traits$species) %>%
  pivot_longer(-species, names_to = "source_order", values_to = "fraction") %>%
  mutate(
    repeat_order = if_else(
      source_order %in% c("LTR", "LINE", "TIR"),
      source_order,
      "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(species, repeat_order) %>%
  summarise(fraction = sum(fraction), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    repeat_order = factor(repeat_order, levels = c("LTR", "LINE", "TIR", "Other"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, repeat_order) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  mutate(xmax = cumsum(fraction), xmin = lag(xmax, default = 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(overview_tips %>% select(species, y), by = "species")
if (
  nrow(overview_order_composition) != 21L * 4L ||
    any(abs(
      overview_order_composition %>%
        group_by(species) %>%
        summarise(total = sum(fraction), .groups = "drop") %>%
        pull(total) - 1
    ) > 1e-10)
) {
  stop("Figure 1 broad-order compositions must close to one for overlap21")
}
overview_order_colors <- c(
  LTR = GBE_COLORS[["purple"]],
  LINE = GBE_COLORS[["blue"]],
  TIR = GBE_COLORS[["green"]],
  Other = GBE_COLORS[["light_gray"]]
)

overview_superfamilies <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT,
    "analyses",
    "01_transposable_elements",
    "data",
    "te_superfamily_composition.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(species %in% overview_traits$species) %>%
  pivot_longer(-species, names_to = "superfamily", values_to = "fraction")
overview_top_superfamilies <- overview_superfamilies %>%
  group_by(superfamily) %>%
  summarise(total_fraction = sum(fraction), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(total_fraction, n = 9, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_fraction)) %>%
  pull(superfamily)
expected_overview_superfamilies <- c(
  "Gypsy",
  "hAT",
  "L2",
  "DIRS",
  "L1",
  "PIF-Harbinger",
  "Mutator",
  "Tc1-mariner",
  "CACTA"
)
if (!setequal(overview_top_superfamilies, expected_overview_superfamilies)) {
  stop("Figure 1 top-nine superfamily set drifted")
}
overview_superfamily_bars <- overview_superfamilies %>%
  filter(superfamily %in% overview_top_superfamilies) %>%
  mutate(
    superfamily = factor(superfamily, levels = overview_top_superfamilies),
    superfamily_index = as.integer(superfamily)
  ) %>%
  left_join(overview_tips %>% select(species, y), by = "species")
overview_superfamily_max <- max(overview_superfamily_bars$fraction)
overview_superfamily_bars <- overview_superfamily_bars %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = superfamily_index - 0.38,
    xmax = superfamily_index + 0.38,
    ymin = y - 0.38,
    ymax = ymin + 0.76 * fraction / overview_superfamily_max
  )
overview_superfamily_frames <- expand_grid(
  species = overview_traits$species,
  superfamily_index = seq_along(overview_top_superfamilies)
) %>%
  left_join(overview_tips %>% select(species, y), by = "species") %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = superfamily_index - 0.45,
    xmax = superfamily_index + 0.45,
    ymin = y - 0.39,
    ymax = y + 0.39
  )

overview_landscape <- read_supp(
  "Supplementary_Data_S12_repeatmasker_divergence_landscape.csv"
) %>%
  filter(
    species %in% overview_traits$species,
    divergence_bin_start_pct < 5
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    repeat_order = if_else(order %in% c("LTR", "LINE", "TIR"), order, "Other")
  ) %>%
  group_by(species, repeat_order) %>%
  summarise(young_repeat_percent = sum(percent_species_hit_bp), .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(
    expand_grid(
      species = overview_traits$species,
      repeat_order = c("LTR", "LINE", "TIR", "Other")
    ),
    by = c("species", "repeat_order")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    young_repeat_percent = replace_na(young_repeat_percent, 0),
    repeat_order = factor(repeat_order, levels = c("LTR", "LINE", "TIR", "Other")),
    order_index = as.integer(repeat_order)
  ) %>%
  left_join(overview_tips %>% select(species, y), by = "species")
if (nrow(overview_landscape) != 21L * 4L || any(is.na(overview_landscape$y))) {
  stop("Figure 1 young-repeat track requires overlap21 by four order groups")
}

Figure 1. Integrated phylogenetic TE landscape across 21 species.

TE diversity context and Bonsai composition representation

Diversity equations and primary filter

For proportions \(p_i\) within a species:

\[ H' = -\sum_i p_i \ln(p_i) \]

\[ D_{GS} = 1 - \sum_i p_i^2 \]

These are natural-log Shannon entropy and the Gini-Simpson index.

Following Wang et al. (2025), the canonical diversity calculation retains each species’s ten most abundant positive TE superfamilies. Those ten proportions are explicitly reclosed to sum to one before calculating natural-log Shannon entropy and the Gini-Simpson index. Wang et al. documented the top-ten scope but did not state whether the retained proportions were reclosed; this report makes our normalization rule explicit. Unresolved aligned-base mass remains separate in S07 as dnaPipeTE classification-accounting QC and is not treated as a diversity category. The 24-shared-superfamily rule below belongs to the Bonsai composition representation and the retained PCA geometry audit.

te_diversity <- read_supp("S08")
superfamily_composition <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data",
    "te_superfamily_composition.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

recomputed_primary <- superfamily_composition %>%
  pivot_longer(-species, names_to = "feature", values_to = "proportion") %>%
  filter(proportion > 0) %>%
  arrange(species, feature) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  slice_max(proportion, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(proportion = proportion / sum(proportion)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_superfamilies_included = n(),
    shannon_entropy = -sum(proportion * log(proportion)),
    gini_simpson = 1 - sum(proportion^2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_primary <- te_diversity %>%
  select(species, n_superfamilies_included, shannon_entropy, gini_simpson) %>%
  arrange(species)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_diversity) == 34L,
  n_distinct(te_diversity$species) == 34L,
  all(te_diversity$n_superfamilies_included == 10L),
  !any(grepl("unresolved", names(te_diversity), ignore.case = TRUE)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_primary, observed_primary, tolerance = 1e-12))
)

te_diversity %>%
  arrange(desc(shannon_entropy)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 4)

Published cross-study top-10 superfamily context

S41 is a descriptive comparison surface containing 118 records: the exact 84 records deposited for Figure 2 by Wang et al. (2025) and 34 current Desmognathus records. The published numerical data were retrieved from Dryad (dataset DOI 10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv) under CC0-1.0 and accompany article DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3.

Both origins report natural-log Shannon and Gini-Simpson diversity over their top 10 TE superfamilies, but the pipelines are different and not method-harmonized. Wang et al. generated the published values from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker annotations; the current Desmognathus rows use the same canonical S08 reclosed calculations from retry-averaged dnaPipeTE compositions. Current genome sizes are conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not direct species C-values. This is descriptive cross-study context only; no pooled regression or hypothesis test is performed.

cross_study_diversity <- read_supp("S41")

origin_counts <- cross_study_diversity %>%
  count(data_origin) %>%
  tibble::deframe()
inclusion_counts <- cross_study_diversity %>%
  count(figure_inclusion) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

stopifnot(
  nrow(cross_study_diversity) == 118L,
  n_distinct(cross_study_diversity$source_record_id) == 118L,
  identical(
    as.integer(origin_counts[c("wang2025_published", "desmognathus_current")]),
    c(84L, 34L)
  ),
  identical(
    as.integer(inclusion_counts[c(
      "published_scatter_and_group", "published_group_only",
      "current_scatter_and_group", "current_group_only"
    )]),
    c(11L, 73L, 21L, 13L)
  ),
  setequal(
    cross_study_diversity$metric_scope,
    c(
      "published_top10_superfamilies_repeatmodeler_repeatmasker",
      "current_top10_superfamilies_dnapipete_retry_averaged"
    )
  )
)

cross_study_diversity %>%
  select(
    data_origin, scientific_name, comparison_group, genome_size_gb,
    shannon_top10_superfamilies, gini_simpson_top10_superfamilies,
    metric_scope, figure_inclusion
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

Shared CLR composition and retained PCA audit

The Bonsai representation and PCA audit use the same retry-averaged superfamily compositions: retain features positive in all 34 TE species, close each row, and apply the centered log-ratio transformation:

\[ \operatorname{clr}(p_{ij}) = \ln(p_{ij}) - \frac{1}{D}\sum_{k=1}^{D}\ln(p_{ik}) \]

For the supplementary PCA audit, columns are centered and an unscaled SVD is fit. There is no zero replacement in the retained 24-superfamily matrix. CR1, Chapaev, Dada, Ginger, and Merlin fail the ubiquitous-feature gate. Their presence does not determine diversity inclusion, which instead uses each species’s abundance-ranked top ten.

te_scores <- read_supp("S09")
te_variance <- read_supp("S10")
te_loadings <- read_supp("S11")
feature_prevalence <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data",
    "te_feature_prevalence.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

retained_superfamilies <- feature_prevalence %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", pca_included)
excluded_superfamilies <- feature_prevalence %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", !pca_included)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_scores) == 34L,
  nrow(te_variance) == 23L,
  nrow(te_loadings) == 24L,
  nrow(retained_superfamilies) == 24L,
  setequal(
    excluded_superfamilies$feature,
    c("CR1", "Chapaev", "Dada", "Ginger", "Merlin")
  )
)

excluded_superfamilies %>%
  select(
    feature, n_species_positive, prevalence_fraction,
    minimum_proportion, maximum_proportion, pca_exclusion_reason
  )

No final sensitivity analysis asks whether forcing CR1 or Chapaev into the shared-feature representation changes support; the report does not invent one.

Bonsai publication representation and exact validation

Figure 2 uses the pinned Bonsai fit to the shared 24-superfamily CLR matrix. S42 binds all 34 tree tips to the expert reproductive-strategy annotation, and S43 binds the exact fixed-tree permutation and bounded feature-resampling statistics shown in the figure.

bonsai_tips <- read_supp("S42")
bonsai_validation <- read_supp("S43")

strategy_counts <- bonsai_tips %>%
  count(reproductive_strategy) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

stopifnot(
  nrow(bonsai_tips) == 34L,
  identical(
    as.integer(strategy_counts[c(
      "aquatic_eggs", "direct_development",
      "terrestrial_eggs_aquatic_larvae"
    )]),
    c(7L, 3L, 24L)
  ),
  nrow(bonsai_validation) == 3L,
  all(bonsai_validation$feature_bootstrap_replicates == 200L),
  identical(
    as.integer(bonsai_validation$feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_count),
    c(55L, 70L, 2L)
  ),
  all(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_observed_steps == 2L),
  all(abs(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_null_mean_steps - 9.41320413) < 1e-8),
  all(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_p_value == 0.00001),
  all(bonsai_validation$global_fitch_p_value_holm == 0.00009)
)

bonsai_validation %>%
  select(
    strategy_label, group_n, full_fit_edge_delimited,
    fixed_tree_smallest_side_p_value_holm,
    feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_count,
    feature_bootstrap_replicates,
    feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_fraction
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 3, columns = 7)

The rooted Newick is a serialization of a non-phylogenetic TE-composition representation: branch length is fitted diffusion time and the display root has no phylogenetic meaning. Strategy labels were supplied after review of the initial PCA. Localization is therefore post hoc and does not establish causation or phylogenetically independent association. Feature resampling perturbs the 24 correlated compositional coordinates; it is not a biological-specimen bootstrap.

Exact ggplot code and current figure

# Figure 2: TE diversity and the Bonsai TE-composition representation.
te_diversity <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S08_te_diversity.csv") %>%
  select(
    species,
    n_superfamilies_included,
    shannon_entropy,
    gini_simpson
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(shannon_entropy, gini_simpson),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "diversity_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      recode(
        metric,
        shannon_entropy = "Shannon entropy",
        gini_simpson = "Gini-Simpson index"
      ),
      levels = c("Shannon entropy", "Gini-Simpson index")
    )
  )
diversity_counts <- te_diversity %>% count(metric)
if (
  nrow(te_diversity) != 68L ||
  n_distinct(te_diversity$species) != 34L ||
    any(te_diversity$n_superfamilies_included != 10L) ||
    nrow(diversity_counts) != 2L ||
    !all(diversity_counts$n == 34L)
) {
  stop("The TE34 top-10-superfamily diversity audit requires 34 species per metric")
}
te_annotations <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S42_te_bonsai_tip_annotations.csv")
te_validation <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S43_te_bonsai_strategy_validation.csv")
bonsai_tree_path <- file.path(
  DATA,
  "trees",
  "te34_bonsai_composition_tree_with_feature_support.nwk"
)
bonsai_tree <- ladderize(read.tree(bonsai_tree_path), right = FALSE)

if (
  Ntip(bonsai_tree) != 34L ||
    Nnode(bonsai_tree) != 33L ||
    !is.rooted(bonsai_tree) ||
    !is.binary(bonsai_tree) ||
    any(bonsai_tree$edge.length < 0) ||
    nrow(te_annotations) != 34L ||
    !setequal(bonsai_tree$tip.label, te_annotations$species) ||
    !identical(
      unname(sort(as.integer(table(te_annotations$reproductive_strategy)))),
      sort(c(7L, 24L, 3L))
    ) ||
    nrow(te_validation) != 3L ||
    any(te_validation$feature_bootstrap_replicates != 200L) ||
    n_distinct(te_validation$global_fitch_observed_steps) != 1L ||
    unique(te_validation$global_fitch_observed_steps) != 2L
) {
  stop("Figure 2 requires the exact validated 34-tip Bonsai publication release")
}

bonsai_tip_count <- Ntip(bonsai_tree)
bonsai_node_x <- node.depth.edgelength(bonsai_tree)
bonsai_node_y <- node.height(bonsai_tree)
bonsai_horizontal <- tibble(
  parent = bonsai_tree$edge[, 1],
  child = bonsai_tree$edge[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    x = bonsai_node_x[parent],
    xend = bonsai_node_x[child],
    y = bonsai_node_y[child],
    yend = bonsai_node_y[child]
  )
bonsai_vertical <- tibble(parent = sort(unique(bonsai_tree$edge[, 1]))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x = bonsai_node_x[parent],
    ymin = min(bonsai_node_y[bonsai_tree$edge[bonsai_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]]),
    ymax = max(bonsai_node_y[bonsai_tree$edge[bonsai_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]])
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
bonsai_tips <- tibble(
  node = seq_len(bonsai_tip_count),
  species = bonsai_tree$tip.label,
  x = bonsai_node_x[seq_len(bonsai_tip_count)],
  y = bonsai_node_y[seq_len(bonsai_tip_count)]
) %>%
  left_join(te_annotations, by = "species", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(
    reproductive_strategy = factor(
      reproductive_strategy,
      levels = te_strategy_levels
    )
  )

descendant_tips <- function(node) {
  if (node <= bonsai_tip_count) return(bonsai_tree$tip.label[[node]])
  children <- bonsai_tree$edge[bonsai_tree$edge[, 1] == node, 2]
  unlist(lapply(children, descendant_tips), use.names = FALSE)
}
strategy_groups <- split(te_annotations$species, te_annotations$reproductive_strategy)
all_bonsai_tips <- bonsai_tree$tip.label
bonsai_nodes <- tibble(
  node = bonsai_tip_count + seq_len(Nnode(bonsai_tree)),
  x = bonsai_node_x[bonsai_tip_count + seq_len(Nnode(bonsai_tree))],
  y = bonsai_node_y[bonsai_tip_count + seq_len(Nnode(bonsai_tree))],
  support = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(bonsai_tree$node.label))
) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    focal_strategy = {
      side <- descendant_tips(node)
      matches <- names(strategy_groups)[vapply(
        strategy_groups,
        function(group) {
          setequal(side, group) || setequal(setdiff(all_bonsai_tips, side), group)
        },
        logical(1)
      )]
      if (length(matches) == 1L) matches[[1]] else NA_character_
    },
    support_label = if_else(
      !is.na(support) & (support >= 50 | !is.na(focal_strategy)),
      paste0(round(support), "%"),
      NA_character_
    ),
    support_colour = if_else(
      is.na(focal_strategy),
      GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]],
      te_strategy_colors[focal_strategy]
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
bonsai_cladewise_edges <- reorder.phylo(bonsai_tree, "cladewise")$edge
bonsai_topology_depth <- numeric(bonsai_tip_count + Nnode(bonsai_tree))
bonsai_root <- setdiff(bonsai_cladewise_edges[, 1], bonsai_cladewise_edges[, 2])
if (length(bonsai_root) != 1L) stop("Bonsai topology display requires one root")
for (edge_index in seq_len(nrow(bonsai_cladewise_edges))) {
  parent <- bonsai_cladewise_edges[edge_index, 1]
  child <- bonsai_cladewise_edges[edge_index, 2]
  bonsai_topology_depth[child] <- bonsai_topology_depth[parent] + 1
}
bonsai_tip_x <- max(bonsai_topology_depth) + 0.5
bonsai_topology_horizontal <- tibble(
  parent = bonsai_tree$edge[, 1],
  child = bonsai_tree$edge[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    x = bonsai_topology_depth[parent],
    xend = if_else(child <= bonsai_tip_count, bonsai_tip_x, bonsai_topology_depth[child]),
    y = bonsai_node_y[child],
    yend = bonsai_node_y[child]
  )
bonsai_topology_vertical <- bonsai_vertical %>%
  mutate(x = bonsai_topology_depth[parent])
bonsai_topology_tips <- bonsai_tips %>% mutate(x = bonsai_tip_x)
bonsai_topology_nodes <- bonsai_nodes %>%
  mutate(x = bonsai_topology_depth[node]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(focal_strategy))
if (
  length(bonsai_root) != 1L ||
    nrow(bonsai_topology_horizontal) != 66L ||
    nrow(bonsai_topology_vertical) != 33L ||
    nrow(bonsai_topology_nodes) != 2L
) {
  stop("Figure 2 topology display must retain 34 tips and the two exact strategy edges")
}

te_association_tests <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT,
    "analyses",
    "01_transposable_elements",
    "data",
    "te_pca_trait_association_tests.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
te_strategy_permanova <- te_association_tests %>%
  filter(test_id == "reproductive_strategy_permanova")
te_strategy_permdisp <- te_association_tests %>%
  filter(test_id == "reproductive_strategy_permdisp")
if (
  nrow(te_strategy_permanova) != 1L ||
    nrow(te_strategy_permdisp) != 1L ||
    te_strategy_permanova$n_species != 34L ||
    te_strategy_permanova$p_value != 0.00001 ||
    te_strategy_permdisp$p_value <= 0.05
) {
  stop("Figure 2 requires the released post-hoc strategy association tests")
}

te_b <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(
    data = bonsai_topology_horizontal,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    linewidth = GBE_LINE_MM,
    lineend = "square",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = bonsai_topology_vertical,
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = ymin, yend = ymax),
    linewidth = GBE_LINE_MM,
    lineend = "square",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = bonsai_topology_tips,
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = reproductive_strategy, shape = reproductive_strategy),
    size = 1.85,
    stroke = 0.45,
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = bonsai_topology_tips,
    aes(x = x + 0.34, y = y, label = display_species),
    hjust = 0,
    size = GBE_LABEL_SIZE_MM,
    fontface = "italic",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_label(
    data = bonsai_topology_nodes,
    aes(x = x - 0.12, y = y, label = support_label, colour = support_colour),
    hjust = 1,
    size = GBE_LABEL_SIZE_MM,
    linewidth = 0,
    label.padding = unit(0.6, "pt"),
    fill = alpha("white", 0.9),
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = te_strategy_colors,
    breaks = te_strategy_levels,
    labels = te_strategy_labels,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = te_strategy_shapes,
    breaks = te_strategy_levels,
    labels = te_strategy_labels,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(-0.4, bonsai_tip_x + 4.2),
    breaks = NULL,
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, bonsai_tip_count + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    x = "TE-composition topology (fitted branch lengths omitted; not a species phylogeny)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5) +
  theme(
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(3, 13, 3, 3, unit = "pt")
  )

z_value <- qnorm(0.975)
te_recovery <- te_validation %>%
  mutate(
    strategy = factor(strategy, levels = te_strategy_levels),
    strategy_short = factor(
      recode(
        as.character(strategy),
        aquatic_eggs = "Aquatic eggs",
        terrestrial_eggs_aquatic_larvae = "Terrestrial eggs +\naquatic larvae",
        direct_development = "Direct development"
      ),
      levels = rev(c(
        "Aquatic eggs",
        "Terrestrial eggs +\naquatic larvae",
        "Direct development"
      ))
    ),
    denominator = 1 + z_value^2 / feature_bootstrap_replicates,
    interval_center = (
      feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_fraction +
        z_value^2 / (2 * feature_bootstrap_replicates)
    ) / denominator,
    interval_half = z_value * sqrt(
      feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_fraction *
        (1 - feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_fraction) /
        feature_bootstrap_replicates +
        z_value^2 / (4 * feature_bootstrap_replicates^2)
    ) / denominator,
    ci_low = pmax(interval_center - interval_half, 0),
    ci_high = pmin(interval_center + interval_half, 1),
    count_label = sprintf(
      "%d/%d",
      feature_bootstrap_edge_delimited_count,
      feature_bootstrap_replicates
    )
  )

Repeat landscape

The production plot selects the six reported categories with the greatest total aligned bases, combines the remainder as Other, zero-fills every species/category/divergence-bin combination, and gives all 34 species equal weight in the across-species curves. The young-repeat summary uses bins below 5% divergence.

# Figure 3: strategy-stratified RepeatMasker divergence profiles and the full

landscape <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S12_repeatmasker_divergence_landscape.csv")
profile_orders <- c("LTR", "LINE", "TIR")
profile_group_levels <- c(
  "All species (n = 34)",
  "Aquatic eggs (n = 7)",
  "Terrestrial eggs + aquatic larvae (n = 24)",
  "Direct development (n = 3)"
)

  `All species (n = 34)` = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]],
  `Aquatic eggs (n = 7)` = te_strategy_colors[["aquatic_eggs"]],

LTR terminal:internal depth proxy

Gate and IQR replay

An eligible element is at least 3,000 bp long, has an exact TEsorter annotation, is LTR/Gypsy, and has at least five whitespace-delimited DOMAIN|MODEL annotations. The essential filter is inclusive and is computed within species over the 408 eligible elements:

\[ Q1 - 1.5\,IQR \leq T:I \leq Q3 + 1.5\,IQR \]

The independent coverage gate requires positive depth across at least 80% of positions separately in the left LTR, right LTR, and internal region. The primary branch is the intersection of IQR retention and that coverage gate.

ltr_elements <- read_supp("S14")
ltr_species <- read_supp("S15")
ltr_coverage <- read_supp("S16")
ltr_excluded <- read_supp("S17")

count_tesorter_domains <- function(value) {
  text <- trimws(as.character(value))
  if (is.na(value) || text == "" || tolower(text) == "none") return(0L)
  length(strsplit(text, "[[:space:]]+")[[1]])
}

ltr_check <- ltr_elements %>%
  mutate(
    recomputed_domain_count = vapply(Domains, count_tesorter_domains, integer(1)),
    recomputed_domain_gate =
      .data[["element length"]] >= 3000 &
      tesorter_annotation_found &
      Order == "LTR" &
      Superfamily == "Gypsy" &
      recomputed_domain_count >= 5
  )

fences <- ltr_check %>%
  filter(recomputed_domain_gate) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    q1 = quantile(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions, 0.25),
    q3 = quantile(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions, 0.75),
    iqr = q3 - q1,
    lower = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ltr_check <- ltr_check %>%
  left_join(fences, by = "species") %>%
  mutate(
    recomputed_iqr_keep = recomputed_domain_gate &
      ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions >= lower &
      ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions <= upper,
    recomputed_coverage =
      left_ltr_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8 &
      right_ltr_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8 &
      internal_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8,
    recomputed_primary = recomputed_iqr_keep & recomputed_coverage
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(ltr_elements) == 1086L,
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_count == as.integer(ltr_check$domain_count)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate == as.logical(ltr_check$domain_gate_keep)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_iqr_keep == as.logical(ltr_check$iqr_filter_keep)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_coverage == as.logical(ltr_check$coverage_ge_80pct)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_primary == as.logical(ltr_check$primary_ltr_element)),
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate) == 408L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_iqr_keep) == 381L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate & ltr_check$recomputed_coverage) == 407L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_primary) == 380L,
  n_distinct(ltr_check$species[ltr_check$recomputed_primary]) == 30L
)

primary_ltr_species <- ltr_species %>%
  filter(
    analysis_branch == "primary_iqr_filtered_coverage_ge_80pct",
    ratio_median > 0
  ) %>%
  select(
    species, n_elements, ratio_median,
    median_bootstrap_ci_low, median_bootstrap_ci_high,
    fraction_ratio_gt_1,
    median_terminal_positive_coverage_fraction,
    median_internal_positive_coverage_fraction
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ratio_median))

stopifnot(nrow(primary_ltr_species) == 30L)
primary_ltr_species %>% show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

The 1,086-row audit table remains intact; filtering changes branch membership instead of deleting evidence. No canonical between-species omnibus test has been finalized for this corrected 380-element branch, so none is added here.

# Figure 4: terminal:internal LTR deletion-footprint proxy.
ltr <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S15_ltr_terminal_internal_species_robustness.csv") %>%
  filter(analysis_branch == "primary_iqr_filtered_coverage_ge_80pct", ratio_median > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    species_label = species_label(species),
    estimate = log2(ratio_median),
    ci_low = log2(median_bootstrap_ci_low),
    ci_high = log2(median_bootstrap_ci_high)
  )

ltr_tree <- prune_source_tree(ltr$species)

ltr_tip_count <- Ntip(ltr_tree)
ltr_node_count <- Nnode(ltr_tree)
ltr_node_y <- node.height(ltr_tree)
ltr_edges <- reorder.phylo(ltr_tree, "cladewise")$edge
ltr_topology_depth <- numeric(ltr_tip_count + ltr_node_count)
ltr_root <- setdiff(ltr_edges[, 1], ltr_edges[, 2])
if (length(ltr_root) != 1L) stop("Figure 4 LTR tree requires one root")
for (edge_index in seq_len(nrow(ltr_edges))) {
  parent <- ltr_edges[edge_index, 1]
  child <- ltr_edges[edge_index, 2]
  ltr_topology_depth[child] <- ltr_topology_depth[parent] + 1
}
ltr_tip_x <- max(ltr_topology_depth) + 0.5

ltr_tree_horizontal <- tibble(
  parent = ltr_edges[, 1],
  child = ltr_edges[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    x = ltr_topology_depth[parent],
    xend = if_else(child <= ltr_tip_count, ltr_tip_x, ltr_topology_depth[child]),
    y = ltr_node_y[child],
    yend = ltr_node_y[child]
  )
ltr_tree_vertical <- tibble(parent = sort(unique(ltr_edges[, 1]))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x = ltr_topology_depth[parent],
    ymin = min(ltr_node_y[ltr_edges[ltr_edges[, 1] == parent, 2]]),
    ymax = max(ltr_node_y[ltr_edges[ltr_edges[, 1] == parent, 2]])
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
ltr_tree_tips <- tibble(
  node = seq_len(ltr_tip_count),
  species = ltr_tree$tip.label,
  species_label = species_label(ltr_tree$tip.label),
  x = ltr_tip_x,
  y = ltr_node_y[seq_len(ltr_tip_count)]
)
ltr_tree_tips_sorted <- ltr_tree_tips %>% arrange(y)
ltr_tip_y_order <- ltr_tree_tips_sorted$species
ltr_canonical_order <- phylogenetic_species_order(ltr$species)

if (
  ltr_tip_count != 30L ||
    ltr_node_count != 29L ||
    !is.rooted(ltr_tree) ||
    !is.binary(ltr_tree) ||
    !is.ultrametric(ltr_tree, tol = 1e-6) ||
    any(ltr_tree$edge.length < 0) ||
    !setequal(ltr_tree$tip.label, ltr$species) ||
    nrow(ltr_tree_horizontal) != 58L ||
    nrow(ltr_tree_vertical) != 29L ||
    !identical(ltr_tip_y_order, ltr_canonical_order) ||
    !identical(ltr_tree_tips_sorted$y, as.numeric(seq_len(ltr_tip_count)))
) {
  stop("Figure 4 requires the exact rooted 30-tip prune in canonical tip-y order")
}

ltr <- ltr %>%
  left_join(
    ltr_tree_tips %>% select(species, y),
    by = "species",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

ltr_elements <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S14_ltr_terminal_internal_elements.csv") %>%
  filter(primary_ltr_element) %>%
  mutate(
    estimate = log2_ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    ltr_tree_tips %>% select(species, y),
    by = "species",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )
if (nrow(ltr_elements) != 380L || n_distinct(ltr_elements$species) != 30L ||
    any(!is.finite(ltr_elements$estimate)) || any(is.na(ltr_elements$y)) ||
    any(is.na(ltr$y))) {
  stop("Figure 4 must expose the exact 380-element, 30-species primary LTR branch")
}

ltr_element_checks <- ltr_elements %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    element_n = n(),
    element_median = median(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  right_join(
    ltr %>% select(species, n_elements, ratio_median),
    by = "species"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S16_ltr_resource_coverage.csv") %>%
      select(species, n_primary_iqr_filtered_elements),
    by = "species"
  )
if (any(is.na(ltr_element_checks$element_n)) ||
    !all(ltr_element_checks$element_n == ltr_element_checks$n_elements) ||
    !all(ltr_element_checks$n_elements == ltr_element_checks$n_primary_iqr_filtered_elements) ||
    !isTRUE(all.equal(
      ltr_element_checks$element_median,
      ltr_element_checks$ratio_median,
      tolerance = 1e-12,
      check.attributes = FALSE
    ))) {
  stop("Figure 4 element observations, medians, and displayed support must agree")
}

# Draw the tree and raw element-level proxy on a shared continuous tip-y scale.
# This makes the supplied-tree geometry, species labels, observations, and
# species summaries use one canonical row order rather than relying on the
# phylo object's storage order.
ltr_tree_left <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(
    data = ltr_tree_horizontal,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    linewidth = 0.35,
    lineend = "square",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = ltr_tree_vertical,
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = ymin, yend = ymax),
    linewidth = 0.35,
    lineend = "square",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]

Panel b shows the zero-aware terminal:internal LTR depth proxy across the exact 380-element primary branch. Hollow points are element-level observations, blue points are species medians, and horizontal blue intervals are 2,000-replicate element-bootstrap intervals. Elements are not biological replicates, and intervals are conditional on the recovered elements and sequencing resources. Elements were retained inclusively within each species' two-sided 1.5-IQR fences and only when the left LTR, right LTR, and internal region each had at least 80% positive-depth coverage. The primary branch derives from 408 LTR/Gypsy candidates at least 3,000 bp long with at least five correctly parsed TEsorter domain annotations. The dotted line marks equal terminal and internal mean depth (1:1); values to its right point in the direction expected under internal-sequence depletion. The tree supplies context and ordering only; this mapping/deletion-footprint proxy is not a phylogenetic analysis or an estimate of an ectopic-recombination, solo-LTR, or DNA-loss rate.",

)

Cell and nucleus morphology

The object table contains 1,152 frozen reviewed cell-nucleus pairs across 24 species; the report does not silently refilter it. Physical area uses the fixed conversion \(0.0144\;\mu m^2\) per pixel. Species point estimates are medians of the accepted reviewed pairs.

morphology_objects <- read_supp("S18")
morphology_species <- read_supp("S19")
morphology_audit <- read_supp("S20")

recomputed_morphology <- morphology_objects %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_size_cells = n(),
    n_size_images = n_distinct(filename),
    n_size_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    cell_area_um2 = median(cell_area_um2),
    nucleus_area_um2 = median(nuc_area_um2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_morphology <- morphology_species %>%
  select(
    species, n_size_cells, n_size_images, n_size_specimens,
    cell_area_um2, nucleus_area_um2
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

stopifnot(
  nrow(morphology_objects) == 1152L,
  nrow(morphology_species) == 24L,
  all(abs(morphology_objects$cell_area_um2 - morphology_objects$cell_area_px * 0.0144) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(morphology_objects$nuc_area_um2 - morphology_objects$nuc_area_px * 0.0144) < 1e-9),
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_morphology, observed_morphology, tolerance = 1e-9))
)

morphology_species %>%
  arrange(desc(cell_area_um2)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 12)

Seven species are represented by one animal. Intervals are conditional paired-object intervals for the observed reviewed data; they are not population-level among-animal uncertainty intervals.

trait_forest_panel <- function(
  data,
  estimate,
  low,
  high,
  x_label,
  support,
  support_values,
  show_support_legend = TRUE
) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[estimate]], y = y)) +
    geom_segment(
      aes(x = .data[[low]], xend = .data[[high]], yend = y),
      linewidth = 0.48,
      colour = GBE_COLORS[["light_gray"]]
    ) +
    geom_point(
      aes(shape = .data[[support]]),
      size = 1.9,
      stroke = 0.55,
      fill = "white",
      colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = support_values,
      name = NULL,
      guide = if (show_support_legend) guide_legend(nrow = 1) else "none"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 24.5), breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL) +
    theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5) +
    theme(
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      legend.position = if (show_support_legend) "bottom" else "none"
    )
}

Conditional genome size

The Path24 analysis and all paper-facing figures use the released genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored field. Values are expressed in pg/1C on a conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored scale. The intervals propagate the released measurement bootstrap but not uncertainty in the selected assembly anchor; these values are not direct independently measured species C-values.

  all(genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_ci_low <= genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored),
  all(genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_ci_high >= genome_size_traits$genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored)
)

Figure 6 shows frozen exploratory Pagel-lambda PGLS sensitivities. Its fitted lines should not be read as causal relationships, and the conditional genome-size scale should not be mistaken for direct species C-value assays.

# Figure 6: conditional genome size and pairwise Pagel-lambda PGLS sensitivity.
genome_size <- path_traits %>%
  transmute(
    species,
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored,
    genome_size_pg_ci_low,
    genome_size_pg_ci_high,
    n_images = n_genome_size_images,
    n_specimens = n_genome_size_specimens

  left_join(
    read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S24_nuclear_iod_quality_balance.csv") %>%
      select(species, passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds),
    by = "species"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    genome_size_support = case_when(
      !passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds ~ "Quality-balance caution",
      n_images == 1L & n_specimens == 1L ~ "One image and animal",
      TRUE ~ "Balanced multiple-image support"
    )
  )
pair_data <- inner_join(
  genome_size,
  morphology %>% mutate(species = as.character(species)) %>% select(-species_label),
  by = "species"

pgls <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S26_pairwise_pgls_sensitivity.csv")

pgls_panel <- function(data, comparison_id, x, y, x_low, x_high, y_low, y_high, x_label, y_label, colour, shape_variable = NULL) {
  stat <- pgls %>% filter(.data$comparison == .env$comparison_id) %>% slice(1)
  x_values <- data[[x]]
  y_values <- data[[y]]
  x_log <- log10(x_values)
  y_log <- log10(y_values)
  x_sequence <- seq(min(x_values), max(x_values), length.out = 200)
  x_z <- (log10(x_sequence) - mean(x_log)) / sd(x_log)
  predicted_z <- stat$pgls_intercept_z + stat$pgls_standardized_beta * x_z
  model_variance <- stat$pgls_var_intercept + 2 * x_z * stat$pgls_cov_intercept_slope + x_z^2 * stat$pgls_var_slope
  critical <- qt(0.975, stat$pgls_degrees_freedom)
  model <- tibble(
    x = x_sequence,
    fit = 10^(mean(y_log) + sd(y_log) * predicted_z),
    low = 10^(mean(y_log) + sd(y_log) * (predicted_z - critical * sqrt(pmax(model_variance, 0)))),
    high = 10^(mean(y_log) + sd(y_log) * (predicted_z + critical * sqrt(pmax(model_variance, 0))))
  )
  lambda_text <- ifelse(stat$pagel_lambda < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.2f", stat$pagel_lambda))
  p_text <- ifelse(
    stat$pgls_p_value < 0.001,
    "<0.001",
    paste("=", sprintf("%.3f", stat$pgls_p_value))
  )
  annotation <- sprintf(
    "β = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]\nP %s",
    stat$pgls_standardized_beta, stat$pgls_ci_low, stat$pgls_ci_high,
    p_text
  )
  panel <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_ribbon(data = model, aes(x = x, ymin = low, ymax = high), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = colour, alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_line(data = model, aes(x = x, y = fit), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = colour, linewidth = 0.65) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = .data[[y_low]], ymax = .data[[y_high]]), width = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = alpha(colour, 0.35)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = .data[[x_low]], xmax = .data[[x_high]]), orientation = "y", width = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = alpha(colour, 0.35))
  if (is.null(shape_variable)) {
    panel <- panel + geom_point(
      shape = 21,
      size = 1.8,
      stroke = 0.55,
      fill = "white",
      colour = colour
    )
  } else {
    panel <- panel +
      geom_point(
        aes(shape = .data[[shape_variable]]),
        size = 2,
        stroke = 0.55,
        fill = "white",
        colour = colour
      ) +
      scale_shape_manual(
        name = NULL,
        values = c(
          "Balanced multiple-image support" = 21,
          "One image and animal" = 24,
          "Quality-balance caution" = 4
        ),
        labels = c("Balanced support", "One image/animal", "Quality caution")
      )
  }
  panel +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = -Inf,
      y = Inf,
      label = annotation,
      hjust = -0.02,
      vjust = 1.25,
      size = GBE_LABEL_SIZE_MM
    ) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = y_label) +
    theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5)
}

genome_a <- pgls_panel(
  pair_data, "genome_size_vs_nucleus_area", "genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored", "nucleus_area_um2",
  "genome_size_pg_ci_low", "genome_size_pg_ci_high", "nucleus_area_um2_ci_low", "nucleus_area_um2_ci_high",
  "Conditional genome size (pg/1C*)", expression("Nucleus area ("*mu*"m"^2*")"), GBE_COLORS[["blue"]], "genome_size_support"
)

Calibration proof: optical density to conditional genome size

Optical density is defined per nuclear-mask pixel from background and observed intensity; nuclear IOD is the sum of optical density over the mask, not mean optical density. The species estimator is the arithmetic mean of the within-image median IOD values. The retained Path24-median relative audit index is:

\[ IOD_{relative,s} = \frac{\operatorname{mean}_{image} (\operatorname{median}_{nucleus}(IOD))_s} {\operatorname{median}_{species}(IOD_{equal-image})} \]

The paper-facing conditional scale instead fixes D. fuscus to the selected rounded pooled assembly span:

\[ G_{reference,1C} = \frac{16.1\ \mathrm{Gbp}} {0.978\ \mathrm{Gbp\ pg}^{-1}} = 16.462167689\ \mathrm{pg}, \qquad G_s = \frac{IOD_{equal-image,s}}{IOD_{equal-image,fuscus}} G_{reference,1C}. \]

Process_413/specimen 32469 and Process_414/specimen 32470 were author-confirmed as the D. fuscus standards and were stained in the same experimental runs as the unknowns. Their exact standard-to-target run map has not been recovered, and their median IOD values differ by approximately 41%. This unresolved calibration/QC evidence is why the resulting pg/1C scale remains conditional. The relative-IOD fields remain available in S22 for calibration audit, not as the default paper-facing trait.

iod_objects <- read_supp("S21")
iod_species <- read_supp("S22")
iod_images <- read_supp("S23")
iod_balance <- read_supp("S24")
iod_diagnostics <- read_supp("S25")

recomputed_iod <- iod_images %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    iod_equal_image_estimate = mean(image_median_iod),
    n_images = n_distinct(filename),
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
iod_anchor <- median(recomputed_iod$iod_equal_image_estimate)
fuscus_iod <- recomputed_iod %>%
  filter(species == "D. fuscus") %>%
  pull(iod_equal_image_estimate)
genome_size_reference_pg <- unique(iod_species$genome_size_reference_pg)
genome_size_calibration_pg_per_iod <- genome_size_reference_pg / fuscus_iod
recomputed_iod <- recomputed_iod %>%
  mutate(
    relative_iod_index = iod_equal_image_estimate / iod_anchor,
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored =
      iod_equal_image_estimate * genome_size_calibration_pg_per_iod
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_iod <- iod_species %>%
  select(
    species, iod_equal_image_estimate, n_images, n_specimens,
    relative_iod_index, genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

recomputed_balance <- with(
  iod_balance,
  max_abs_standardized_mean_difference <= 0.10 & max_ks_distance <= 0.25
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(iod_objects) == 805L,
  nrow(iod_images) == 51L,
  nrow(iod_species) == 24L,
  length(fuscus_iod) == 1L,
  length(genome_size_reference_pg) == 1L,
  abs(iod_anchor - 950.176112815) < 1e-8,
  abs(genome_size_reference_pg - 16.462167689) < 1e-8,
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_iod, observed_iod, tolerance = 1e-7)),
  identical(
    recomputed_balance,
    as.logical(iod_balance$passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds)
  ),
  sum(!recomputed_balance) == 4L
)

iod_species %>%
  select(
    species, n_nuclei, n_images, n_specimens,
    iod_equal_image_estimate, relative_iod_index,
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored,
    estimate_support, sample_size_support, quality_match_status
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 10)

The calibration quality-balance rule is max |SMD| <= 0.10 and max KS <= 0.25. The four failures remain visible in the released data and by point shape in Figure 6; they are not silently removed.

iod_balance %>%
  arrange(passes_prespecified_balance_thresholds, desc(max_ks_distance)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 10)

Integrated species views

S40 is the exact 21-species TE34-by-Path24 overlap. The join is at species level; genomic and microscopy measurements are not from the same animal.

te_genome_size_overlap <- read_supp("S40")

  show_col_types = FALSE

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_genome_size_overlap) == 21L,
  n_distinct(te_genome_size_overlap$species) == 21L,
  nrow(organismal_traits) == 37L,
  n_distinct(organismal_traits$species) == 37L
)

te_genome_size_overlap %>%
  select(
    species, scientific_name, shannon_entropy, gini_simpson,
    genome_size_pg_fuscus_anchored,

    manual_review_inclusion
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

The expert reproductive-strategy categories are retained as vetted organismal traits, but the interpretation was supplied after review of the initial PCA. Any overlay is therefore post hoc and descriptive, not a confirmatory test.

organismal_traits %>%
  select(
    species, max_svl_mm, development_mode, reproductive_strategy,
    aquaticity_index, microhabitat_class,
    reproductive_strategy_source_id, organismal_source_ids
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

Existing frozen statistical sensitivities

This tab exposes existing frozen exploratory outputs so collaborators can inspect them. It does not promote them to confirmatory manuscript claims. The report does not run the previously discussed ad hoc power, omnibus, or univariate phylogenetic-signal calculations. No final between-species LTR test or diversity-index group test is added here.

The Path24 traits are log10-transformed and sample-standardized for the current three-trait analysis. Pairwise PGLS estimates Pagel’s lambda by maximum likelihood. Genome size is the released conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C trait throughout S04 and S26–S37. The model otherwise contains nucleus area and cell area only; the possible integrated TE/SVL path model has not been specified or fitted.

pairwise_pgls <- read_supp("S26")
path_models <- read_supp("S30")
path_stability <- read_supp("S32")
path_simulation <- read_supp("S36")
path_dsep <- read_supp("S37")

pairwise_pgls %>%
  select(
    comparison, spearman_rho, p_value_descriptive_only,
    pearson_r, pearson_p_value_descriptive_only,
    pgls_standardized_beta, pgls_ci_low, pgls_ci_high,
    pgls_p_value, pagel_lambda, n_species
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 3, columns = 11)
path_models %>%
  filter(analysis_type == "primary") %>%
  arrange(delta_CICc) %>%
  show_table(rows = 10, columns = 12)

The complete frozen outputs S26–S37 are linked in the Downloads tab. Their code authority is analyses/03_phylogenetic_path/run_path_analysis.R.

The formal TE-PCA audit remains a supplementary geometry and clustering audit, separate from the main Bonsai representation and descriptive S08–S11 tables:

te_audit_dir <- file.path(ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data")
te_cluster_diagnostics <- read_csv(
  file.path(te_audit_dir, "te_pca_clustering_diagnostics.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

te_cluster_diagnostics %>%
  select(any_of(c(

te_phylogenetic_tests %>% show_table(rows = 6, columns = 10)

No discrete PCA cluster is accepted. The collaborator Path24 species-tree provenance issue is separate from Bonsai, which is not a species phylogeny. The PCA audit replay command is make te-pca; the Bonsai replay command is make te-bonsai. Neither is rerun while knitting this report.

# Figure 7: conditional genome-size display of the frozen path comparison and calibration.
path_models <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S30_path_model_comparison.csv") %>%
  filter(analysis_type == "primary") %>%
  arrange(delta_CICc) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(
    model_label = gsub("_", " ", model),
    model_label = sub("^genome", "Genome size", model_label),
    model_label = factor(model_label, levels = rev(model_label))
  )
simulation <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S36_path_simulation_calibration.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    generating_label = gsub("_", " ", generating_class),
    generating_label = sub("^genome", "Genome size", generating_label),
    residual_label = recode(residual_regime, iid = "Independent residuals", brownian = "Brownian residuals")
  )

path_a <- ggplot(
  path_models,
  aes(
    delta_CICc,
    model_label,
    colour = globally_supported,
    shape = globally_supported
  )
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.35, colour = GBE_COLORS[["gray"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 1.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = GBE_COLORS[["blue"]], `FALSE` = GBE_COLORS[["vermillion"]]), name = "Global fit", labels = c("Rejected", "Passed")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 17), name = "Global fit", labels = c("Rejected", "Passed")) +
  labs(x = expression(Delta*"CICc from best Path24 model"), y = NULL) +
  theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5)

path_b <- ggplot(
  simulation,
  aes(
    generating_label,
    true_class_top_rate,
    colour = residual_label,
    shape = residual_label,
    group = residual_label
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 1.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.45)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(GBE_COLORS[c("blue", "orange")]), name = "Simulation regime") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = "Simulation regime") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Generating equivalence class", y = "True-class top-model rate") +
  theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 28, hjust = 1))

Figure_7 <- path_a + path_b +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.45, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Auxiliary review figures

These unnumbered figures are displayed in the exact order declared by Publication/figures/AUXILIARY_FIGURE_MANIFEST.csv and remain outside the numbered manuscript-figure sequence.

Wang-style integrated TE-history candidate boundary. Review candidate, not a numbered manuscript figure. Six representatives are selected deterministically from overlap21 conditional genome-size quantiles plus the D. fuscus anchor. Repeat proportions are fractions of aligned RepeatMasker hit bp, not genome occupancy; divergence bins are not insertion ages.

Wang-style TE-diversity candidate boundary. Reproductive-strategy panels are post-hoc descriptive strata. Conditional genome sizes are assembly-anchored IOD-derived estimates. The two direct developers are shown without a regression because n = 2; the other six panels use Pagel-lambda PGLS fits.

Path24 development and phenotype boundary. Descriptive review only: the Path24 tree-aligned view contains 2 direct-development species and 22 aquatic-larval species. D. organi is absent from Path24 because it has no complete phenotype record. No development mode or phenotype is imputed. The picogram track contains conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not direct independently measured species C-values. The supplied tree provenance remains unresolved.

Path DAG equivalence-class reference boundary. The current Path24 analysis scores 10 testable Markov-equivalence classes, and the auxiliary image shows one representative DAG for each class. The saturated 6-member class is omitted because it has no d-separation claim and was not scored. The Genome size node uses the released conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C estimates, not direct species C-value measurements. The same genome-size scale is used across all scored classes. The shown DAGs are representative only and do not orient unique causal arrows.

Cross-study TE-diversity reference boundary. Descriptive cross-study context only; no pooled regression or hypothesis test. Wang et al. (2025) values are the published top-10 TE-superfamily indices from Dryad (dataset DOI 10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv; article DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3; CC0-1.0), generated from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker annotations. Current Desmognathus top-10 indices are reclosed calculations from dnaPipeTE compositions; the pipelines are different and not method-harmonized. Current genome sizes are conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not direct species C-values.

Wang-style integrated TE content and proliferation candidate

Boundary. Review candidate, not a numbered manuscript figure. Six representatives are selected deterministically from overlap21: nearest to the 0%, 20%, 40%, 80%, and 100% conditional genome-size quantiles plus the D. fuscus anchor. Conditional genome size is IOD-derived and not a direct species C-value. Repeat proportions are fractions of aligned RepeatMasker hit bp, not genome occupancy; divergence bins are not insertion ages.

Legend. Panel A prunes the supplied dated species tree to six deterministic overlap21 representatives. Panel B gives conditional D. fuscus-anchored genome size. Panels C-D show aligned-repeat composition for the six most abundant named biological orders plus Other, which includes the Unclassified annotation. Panel E shows zero-filled RepeatMasker divergence profiles on one common percentage scale.

Release status. auxiliary_review_candidate_wang_style_six_representatives

Wang-style TE diversity and genome-size candidate

Boundary. Review candidate, not a numbered manuscript figure. All genome-size values are conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored IOD-derived estimates, not direct species C-values. Reproductive-strategy panels are post-hoc descriptive strata. The two direct developers are shown without a regression because n = 2.

Legend. Rows show the canonical top-ten-superfamily Shannon entropy and Gini-Simpson index. Columns show all 21 overlap species, six aquatic-egg species, 13 terrestrial-egg species with aquatic larvae, and two direct developers. Hollow points are species and horizontal bars are conditional genome-size intervals. Lines and bands are Pagel-lambda PGLS fits and coefficient confidence bands; the n = 2 direct-development panels intentionally have no fit.
